import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns
import matplotlib.ticker as mticker

# Load the dataset
try:
    df = pd.read_csv('data/dogs_zurich.csv')
except FileNotFoundError:
    print("Dataset not found. Please ensure 'data/dogs_zurich.csv' is in the correct directory.")
    exit()

# --- Data Preparation ---

# Clean breed names by capitalizing and stripping whitespace
df['Rasse1Text'] = df['Rasse1Text'].str.strip().str.title()

# Identify the top 10 most common breeds across all years.
# We exclude "Mischling" (mixed breed) as it's a general category,
# to focus on specific breed trends.
top_breeds = df[df['Rasse1Text'] != 'Mischling']['Rasse1Text'].value_counts().nlargest(10).index

# Filter the dataframe to include only the top 10 breeds
df_top_breeds = df[df['Rasse1Text'].isin(top_breeds)]

# Group by year and breed to get the annual count for each of the top breeds
yearly_counts = df_top_breeds.groupby(['StichtagDatJahr', 'Rasse1Text']).size().reset_index(name='count')

# --- Visualization ---

# Set the aesthetic style of the plots
sns.set_theme(style="whitegrid")

# Create the figure and axes
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(16, 10))

# Create the line plot using seaborn
# A well-distinguishable color palette is chosen.
palette = sns.color_palette("tab10", n_colors=10)
lineplot = sns.lineplot(
    data=yearly_counts,
    x='StichtagDatJahr',
    y='count',
    hue='Rasse1Text',
    style='Rasse1Text',  # Use style for different markers, enhancing accessibility
    markers=True,
    dashes=False,
    palette=palette,
    linewidth=2.5,
    markersize=8,
    ax=ax
)

# --- Customization and Labeling for Clarity ---

# Set a clear and informative title
ax.set_title('Popularity Trends of Top 10 Dog Breeds in Zurich', fontsize=22, pad=25, weight='bold', loc='left')
fig.text(0.125, 0.9, 'Annual count of registered dogs for the most common purebreds, excluding mixed breeds.', fontsize=14, color='gray')


# Set axis labels with appropriate font sizes
ax.set_xlabel('Year', fontsize=16, labelpad=15)
ax.set_ylabel('Number of Registered Dogs', fontsize=16, labelpad=15)

# Customize tick parameters for better readability
ax.tick_params(axis='x', labelsize=12)
ax.tick_params(axis='y', labelsize=12)

# Ensure x-axis ticks are integers representing years
ax.xaxis.set_major_locator(mticker.MaxNLocator(integer=True))
plt.xticks(rotation=0)

# Improve the legend
handles, labels = ax.get_legend_handles_labels()
ax.legend(
    handles=handles,
    labels=labels,
    title='Dog Breed',
    bbox_to_anchor=(1.02, 1),
    loc='upper left',
    fontsize=11,
    title_fontsize=13,
    frameon=False
)

# Set y-axis to start from 0
ax.set_ylim(0)

# Despine to remove unnecessary chart borders
sns.despine(left=True, bottom=True)

# Add a subtle grid for easier value reading
ax.grid(axis='y', linestyle='--', alpha=0.7)
ax.grid(axis='x', linestyle=':', alpha=0.5)


# Save the final figure
# bbox_inches='tight' ensures all elements (like the legend) are included
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)
